The show is about middle schoolers, but clearly aimed at adults. Especially adults who have gone trough really difficult puberty. This put it to the difficult spot. Fans of serious adult work skipped it because it set in school and fans of shonen stories watched first episode and did start to ridicule it, expecting another OreImo.

I have never scoffed at characters' problems and how they are small and unimportant. Partly because they are not so for them, and partly because I felt for the characters judging everyone around them as small, tiring and conceited. It portrays teenage angst brilliantly.

The story develops slowly, relies heavily on the atmosphere in the middle of the rusty, run-down and ugly city. This is the only work that made me sit on the edge of my seat, heart beating at the sight of two middle-schoolers walking, holding hands.

The rotoscoped animation fits the tone as a glove. It is ugly, deep in uncanny valley and damn perfect. It is the source of a ridicule (Aku no Potato is the most common insult to the series) and its low success. Shame.

The anime is an adaptation of a manga, yet due to excellent atmosphere, slow pacing and experimental animation surpasses it. Oh, and music. God the music.

So, who will like it: People who like slowish stories and are no strangers to atmosphere-oriented work. It bears resemblance to Mamoru Oshii's works like Jin-Roh or Ghost in the Shell movies, Kotonoha no Niwa (although that used resources to make a world seem more beautiful, Aku no Hana to make it more ugly), Lars von Trier's Dogville and Antichrist, Lynch's Eraserhead and Inland Empire. As you can see, those works have little in common. There is nothing quite like Aku no Hana, I had to reach out to similar atmosphere rather than similar setting, themes or story.

Who will not like it: Those who find Shigneki no Kyoujin example of how anime should be made, and whose best of all time is Fullmetal Alchemist and Suzumia Haruhi no Yuutsu. Characters are flawed and actually behave like adolescents, so if you thought that Shinji in Neon Genesis Evangelion was just a pussy because he did not go in Rambo mode, spewing tough one liners and bravely charging at enemies you will hate the protagonist Kasuga. Kasuga is actually a coward and that makes him an interesting character, as well as allows plot to be pushed forward.
